title: parallel tool returns reconciliation and retry choreography for OpenAI-compat
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: Customers are building multi-tool workflows where the model fan-outs tool calls in parallel and expects a single, deterministic structured injection back into the next model turn. We observed two classes of problems in production: (1) non-deterministic ordering and partial/overlapping streamed tool outputs which break structured output parsing, and (2) retry storms and duplicated results when a subset of parallel tool calls fail transiently. This PR introduces a reconciliation layer and retry choreography to make parallel tool-calling ergonomics reliable and OpenAI-compat friendly.

What this PR does (high-level): Adds a Reconciler component that: 1) accepts concurrent tool responses (streamed or final) and materializes a canonical merged representation; 2) enforces deterministic injection ordering via a reconcile_id and explicit injection_strategy; 3) implements per-tool retry/backoff and a short-circuit policy for "first-success" strategies to reduce tail latency and cost. On the API surface we add opt-in request flags for OpenAI-compat requests: "reconcile_id", "injection_strategy" (values: "merge", "first-success", "serial"), and "max_retries_per_tool". SDK helpers expose an ergonomic call_tools(...) helper that returns the reconciled structured output and metadata for diagnostics.

Key design points: - Deterministic ordering: callers can opt to preserve the generation order with "serial" or allow a merge strategy that combines outputs by semantic slot. Reconciler uses a stable slot ordering derived from the call graph to avoid flakiness. - Streaming stability: partial streamed chunks from tools are buffered and reassembled in a small in-memory window (configurable via reconcile_window_ms) before they are forwarded as a single atomic injection event to the language model. This prevents the model from seeing interleaved partial payloads. - Retry choreography: per-tool backoff is jittered and bounded; the reconciler tracks idempotency keys provided by tools to dedupe retries. For "first-success" strategy we short-circuit remaining tools once a minimum-success threshold is reached. - OpenAI compatibility: function-calling style metadata is preserved; reconciled outputs are emitted as valid function-call payloads (name + arguments) so existing OpenAI-compat clients can consume results without extra parsing changes. - Observability: events, per-tool latencies, retry counts, and reconciliation decisions are emitted to existing traces/metrics. We added tracing tags reconcile_id and injection_strategy.

API changes and backwards compatibility: - New optional fields on the inference request JSON: "reconcile_id" (string), "injection_strategy" (string), "max_retries_per_tool" (int), "reconcile_window_ms" (int). Defaults maintain current behavior (no reconciliation; naive injection) so this is opt-in and non-breaking. - SDK helpers: python and typescript convenience functions wrap the new fields and handle streaming reassembly. Existing SDK call sites that don't opt in see no change.

Implementation notes and tradeoffs: - Reconciler lives in runtime/reconciler.py and sits between the tool-runner and the streaming response multiplexer. It maintains an ephemeral in-memory buffer keyed by reconcile_id; for large outputs we spill to disk using the existing chunk-store utility to avoid OOM. - To avoid increased tail latency we aggressively favor optimistic short-circuits under "first-success" and expose per-request thresholds. - We added integration tests that replay production failures (partial stream cuts, duplicated tool callbacks) to assert deterministic reconciled outputs.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on a 4xA100 stack show median additional latency of ~4ms for reconciliation in the common case (small tool outputs) and 95th percentile increase of ~12-18ms when buffering larger streamed payloads. Cost/regressions: we observed negligible tokenization overhead; the main cost is slightly increased CPU for reassembly under heavy fan-out which is bounded by a configurable concurrency limit.

Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind runtime flag reconcile.enabled=false by default. - Canary rollout to 10% of hosted traffic with a revert window of 48 hours. - SDK release (python/ts) coordinated: minor semver bump with new helper exposed. - Docs/compat: update OpenAI-compat page with examples showing function-call style reconciled results and migration notes.

Testing: Unit tests for reconciler logic, end-to-end integration tests that validate deterministic injection and retry backoff behavior, and performance runbooks added to benchmarks/. CI: added a new workflow to exercise long-lived streaming reconnection scenarios.

Notes for reviewers: focus on idempotency/dedupe correctness (reconciler/keys), spike protection under many concurrent reconcile_ids, and the SDK ergonomics (is call_tools intuitive?). Also validate the OpenAI-compat output shape in docs/openai_compat/tool-calling.md.

Related: ENG-9876 (design), SUP-2219 (customer incident), ENG-10012 (retry policy work).

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can you explain how we guarantee stable ordering across retries? Stateful slot ordering looks tricky when callers fan-out dynamically.

Author (Aisha Khan): We derive the stable slot order from the call graph emitted with the request (tools are assigned deterministic indices). Retries are keyed to the original slot index so dedupe is deterministic.
Ravi Singh: Need circuit-breaker so a misbehaving tool doesn't drag reconciler memory. Also prefer upper bounds on in-flight reconcile_ids.
Author: Added a per-reconciler in-flight cap and eviction policy; spelled this out in runtime/reconciler.py and added metrics. See commit b27d4f1.
Zoe Martinez: SDK ergonomics look good, but please add an example that shows streaming injection + structured function-call output.
Author: Added expanded examples and a migration snippet in docs/openai_compat/tool-calling.md.
Nadia Chen: CI flake on streaming reconnect test; was due to test harness timing. I reran and all checks passed.
Liam O'Connor: Approve after the small nit on naming (reconcile_window_ms -> reconcile_window_ms) fixed.
Author: Fixed naming nit and added a one-line changelog entry.
release_notes: Add reconciler for deterministic multi-tool injection and retry choreography. Opt-in via request flags: reconcile_id, injection_strategy, max_retries_per_tool. SDK helpers provided for python and typescript.
notes: Feature gated; will monitor per-tool retry metrics and reconcile buffer memory during canary.
